note: Primary study and follow-up literature confirm hyperphagia and obesity occur in a distinct subset ('several cases' or 'in some patients', reminiscent of Prader-Willi syndrome) of LRRC7 cohort individuals.

evidence.text: In a cohort of 33 individuals with dominant neurodevelopmental disorder due to LRRC7 variants, the authors noted hyperphagia associated with obesity in several cases, starting between 4 and 10 years of age and resembling Prader-Willi syndrome.

source.title: Variants in LRRC7 lead to intellectual disability, autism, aggression and abnormal eating behaviors
source.quote: As a third remarkable phenotype, we noted hyperphagia associated with obesity, starting between 4 and 10 years of age. Case descriptions are reminiscent of cases of Prader-Willi

evidence.text: Subsequent report notes that hyperphagia and class-II obesity are reported in a subset of older individuals with LRRC7-related neurodevelopmental disorder.

source.title: Further Evidence for LRRC7 Gene Involvement in Neurodevelopmental Disorder: A Novel Variant
source.quote: Interestingly, hyperphagia and class- II obesity—reported in a subset of older individuals, … Our findings thus expand the mutational and phenotypic spectrum of LRRC7- related disorders
